user_questions.question: Three scope questions: (1) How should POS items be matched to Salesforce? Options: a scheduled job per storefront calling the POS API and upserting Menu_Item__c by a new POS external ID (no external ID exists today on any menu object), or match by Name. (2) When an item disappears from the POS, should the sync set Menu_Item__c.Available__c = false, delete the record, or leave it? (3) Which Menu__c should synced items go into? Options: one Menu__c per POS menu keyed by a POS menu ID, or a single existing menu per storefront (2 storefronts already have more than one menu; 73 items have no menu).
user_questions.simulated_answer: (1) Scheduled job per storefront calling the POS API, upserting Menu Items by external id. (2) No preference; use your recommended default. (3) No preference; use your recommended default.

user_questions.question: Each merchant has its own Square or Toast account and no POS credential exists in the org. Should the sync use one shared Named Credential per provider, or a per-storefront credential (Storefront__c.POS_Credential_Name__c naming a Named Credential created at merchant onboarding)?
user_questions.simulated_answer: No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: Step 5 allows one extra scope message for a new blocking fork, but does not say whether the per-merchant credential model (a question that surfaced only after I) is 'new'; I treated it as new.
The response-handling table counts a split as one retry, but run.json kinds have no way to mark the second half of a split (T after the R retry); I labelled it 't'.

Rule 3 says reject proposals that contradict documented Salesforce behavior, but gives no rule for proposals that contradict documented third-party API behavior (Square has no /v2/locations/{id}/menus endpoint); I handled it as an assumption plus a Section 8 conflict.
org-verification.md has no query for ExternalCredential; the standard-API query is rejected, so absence of Square/Toast External Credentials could not be verified with the allowed commands.
The skill gives no guidance on org-edition limits (Developer Edition caps chained Queueable depth at 5) that change the design; I had to reshape AskCoworker's Queueable design from general knowledge.
Section 8 must hold user decisions, conflicts, corrections, and open decisions in one numbered list, which makes it long; there is no guidance on separating resolved items from open ones.
